articles.headline: The Five-Minute Rule Beats Procrastination, Students Say
articles.dek: Can’t make yourself start? Commit to five minutes and see what actually happens.
articles.author: Maya Chen
body: Ask around and you’ll hear the same trick from students who’ve stopped dreading their assignments: promise yourself just five minutes. Not the whole worksheet, not the whole essay — five minutes, with permission to stop after.

The logic is simple. Starting is almost always harder than continuing, and a five-minute promise is small enough that it doesn’t trigger the usual wave of dread. Most students who try it report the same thing: once the five minutes are up, they keep going anyway.
It won’t make homework fun. But it turns a mountain into a doorway, and a doorway is a lot easier to walk through.
tips: Set an actual timer for five minutes — no more.
Choose the smallest possible first step, not the hardest part.
If you stop at five minutes, that still counts as a win.
